name: Louvain breaks equal gains by the label of the node a community started from
why: The path e - b - a - c - d has two partitions of equal modularity, {a,c,d}{b,e} and {a,b,e}{c,d}; which one is returned is decided by the tie rule alone. m = 4, degrees a, b, c = 2 and d, e = 1, so gain(c) = k_in(c) - tot(c) * k / 8.

queries.why: Pass 1: a sees b and c at gain 1 - 2*2/8 = 0.5 each and joins the smaller label, b's. b then prefers e (0.75 over 0.5) and leaves a alone under label b; c joins d (0.75), and d and e stay. Pass 2: a sees {c,d} (label d) and {b,e} (label e) at gain 1 - 3*2/8 = 0.25 each and joins label d, the smaller, even though b is the smallest member of {b,e}. Q = 2/4 - (5/8)^2 + 1/4 - (3/8)^2 = 0.21875.
